root.name: Benoni Defense: Fianchetto Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 c5 4. d5 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. Nc3 g6 7. g3

overview: White develops the king's bishop on g2 and castles instead of building the e4/f4 centre, so the e4 break stays in reserve. Black castles, plays ...Re8, ...Nbd7 and ...a6 and prepares ...b5 or ...Nh5 and ...f5. The play is strategic: White restrains the queenside break while Black seeks activity on the e- and c-files.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the d5 space advantage and play e4 or Nd2 at the right moment
Neutralise ...b5 with a4 and put pressure on the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...b5 on the queenside, using the half-open e- and c-files

typical_structures.structure: Benoni structure: White pawn on d5 versus Black c5/d6, White majority in the centre and kingside, Black majority on the queenside

character.notes: Less forcing than the Modern or Four Pawns Benoni, but the asymmetric structure still gives Black counter-chances and White space.

soundness.notes: A solid, long-standing way for White to meet the Benoni.

structure.notes: Fixed asymmetric centre; Black presses along the e- and c-files.

approach.notes: A mainstream choice against the Benoni, standard.

level.notes: Needs good timing of e4 and ...b5, but less forcing theory than other Benoni lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: Black's ...Nh5 and ...f5 plans
sublines_that_differ.how: Black goes after the kingside rather than the queenside.

character.reason: Strategic Benoni with sharp potential but White's set-up cuts most forcing lines.

soundness.reason: A mainstream line for both sides.

structure.reason: A fixed asymmetric centre pressed along the e- and c-files.

approach.reason: A mainstream line against the Benoni.

plans.reason: White's d5 space, Black's ...b5 break and the g2 bishop define the structure.
